rationale: The internal logic is sound (INDICATOR(NEG(coverage), -1) does isolate coverage<1 firms and the sign direction is coherent), but this is essentially the archive's already-tested `adequacy_vs_all_current_claims` / `liquidity_sources_over_uses` structure with the continuous low-coverage weight discretized into a binary gate, i.e. a cosmetic variant of a leg that has repeatedly produced strong FMB slopes and null alpha.

Frequency of material capital raises is a genuinely new dimension relative to the archive's magnitude- and volatility-based dependence measures, the construction is internally consistent with the stated negative sign, and coarseness (four values, heavy ties) is a manageable rather than fatal concern.

This is a sample-splicing device rather than a new economic hypothesis — it mechanically stitches two already-evaluated signals (`internal_vs_external_wall_coverage` and `earnings_based_wall_coverage`) and, because oancf is missing largely by reporting era, the resulting cross-section ranks non-comparable proxies whose mix shifts over time, confounding the mechanism test with a regime split.

DELTA(ceq) minus (ni − dvt) is the standard balance-sheet net equity issuance measure, so with a negative expected sign this is a direct rediscovery of the published net-share-issuance / composite-equity-issuance anomaly, merely reweighted by a leverage rank.

The two legs are known anomalies in their known directions — profitability/retained earnings (positive) minus net equity issuance (negative) — so a positive spread is close to guaranteed by construction and would not identify the internal-versus-external liquidity mechanism it claims to test.

Collateral capacity is a legitimately new conditioning dimension and the sign logic is coherent, but the expression is structurally the fifth instance of centred-dependence-leg × monotone non-negative rank weight, a form that has already delivered large FMB t-stats with no portfolio alpha, so it is unlikely to resolve the archive's existing FMB/alpha disagreement.
